Implementation — PR 5 — doc-examples-diagnostics-ipw

Source: implementation.md

Branch: docs/examples-diagnostics-ipw Plan: plans/doc-examples-overhaul.md — Task 6 (PR 5, diagnostics and ipw())

Write surface

  • R/effective_sample_size.R — modified (@examples only: added #> comment)
  • R/weight_variability.R — modified (@examples only: added #> comment)
  • R/summarize_weights.R — modified (@examples only: added two #> blocks)
  • R/ipw.R — modified (@examples only: full rewrite, 111 lines to 45)
  • man/effective_sample_size.Rd — generated by devtools::document()
  • man/weight_variability.Rd — generated by devtools::document()
  • man/summarize_weights.Rd — generated by devtools::document()

Summary

  • Added #> expected-output comments to effective_sample_size(), weight_variability(), and both summarize_weights() scenarios, pasted from real pkgload::load_all() output; all values matched D5’s table with no discrepancy.
  • Rewrote ipw()’s @examples from 111 lines to exactly 45: five scenarios (GSS both interfaces, CPS survey_replicate, NPORS three missing_method values, GEE, known population size), each assigning and using its result via summarize_weights()/calibrate()/nrow().
  • Closed the ipw() GEE dataset gap per D4: replaced inline synthetic data.frame() construction with npors_2025_clean + wt_pop + strata = stratum; deleted nps_gee, ref_gee_df, ref_gee, and the direct surveycore::survey_taylor() call. No inline data.frame construction remains in R/ipw.R’s examples.
  • Seeded the mice sub-case via mice_args = list(seed = 42L); kept the requireNamespace("mice", quietly = TRUE) guard (load-bearing — mice is not installed in this worktree).
  • Removed all four redundant data() calls in R/ipw.R (LazyData: true makes them dead code); added tests/testthat/test-example-values.R guarding all three diagnostics’ #> comments (ungrouped and by = sex), 31 assertions, all passing.

Task checklist

Signals raised

None. No HOLD.

One deliberate deviation from a literal reading of Task 6, reported per instructions: the GSS scenario (gss_2024 as reference) is NOT pre-filtered for its own NA in sex/age_f3, so surveywts_warning_ipw_reference_na_omitted fires three times across the block (once per call that uses gss_ref), uncommented. Task 6’s checklist only names surveywts_warning_ipw_data_na_omitted for the NPORS “omit” sub-case; it says nothing about this reference-side warning. Leaving gss_2024 unfiltered reproduces D6’s own audited count exactly (“surveywts_warning_ipw_reference_na_omitted (x3) … gss_2024 has NA in sex and age_f3 (112 rows)”), so this reads as the plan’s intended, pre-existing behavior rather than a defect to fix — but it does mean the GSS scenario is not fully silent. D2’s claim that the ipw() downstream chain is “silent” is read here as describing the two downstream calls (summarize_weights() + calibrate()), not the ipw() call itself, since running it literally shows the reference-side warning firing on the very first call. Flagging this reading for review rather than silently resolving it either way.

CRAN compliance

Notes for tester

  • The ipw() @examples block is exactly 45 lines (the plan’s hard cap), counted the way the plan counts: every #' line after @examples to the next roxygen tag. There is no headroom in that count — any future edit to R/ipw.R’s examples should re-measure rather than assume slack.
  • air format --check passes on all four touched R/ files and the new test file; roxygen comments are untouched by air per code-style.md §1.
  • Ran devtools::test() once (full suite): FAIL 0 | WARN 783 | SKIP 6 | PASS 3706, no regressions. The warning count is pre-existing package behavior (unseeded draws, third-party messages), not something this PR changed.
  • rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck() was run once with _R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_=false under .claude/skills/.../scratchpad, never inside the repo.
